Research has shown that rituals and repetitive experiences can shape our attitudes and behaviors through a process called "habituation." This can lead to a greater sense of empathy, compassion, and forgiveness, as you become more attuned to the needs and feelings of others. The shared rituals and traditions create a sense of belonging and identity, which can strengthen your relationships with family, friends, and community members. It's also worth noting that the act of fasting during Lent can be a powerful tool for self-reflection and personal growth. By temporarily abstaining from certain comforts or pleasures, you may become more aware of your own needs and desires, as well as the needs and struggles of others. This can lead to a greater sense of gratitude, humility, and compassion. Overall, going through the same experiences every year can indeed change how someone thinks about what they owe others.
